title: Anna's MOE btanimoto/ctanimoto reference vs Pyxis stock search (attributed record, not a reproducibility target)
attributedTo: Anna (CompChem), reported 2026-09-12 via email quoted by the product owner

metricDefinitions.btanimoto: Deduplicate the feature lists, then set Jaccard.
metricDefinitions.ctanimoto: Sum(x_i*y_i) / (Sum(x_i^2) + Sum(y_i^2) - Sum(x_i*y_i)) using feature frequencies.

notes: Her MOE btanimoto hit count was reported as ~30; ids above are the 30 she listed, in her given order.

Anna's exact MOE fingerprint definition is UNKNOWN (no MOE version or settings metadata exists anywhere; the source TSV carries 11 FP:* columns and none is identified as the searched one), so fingerprintIdentified is false.

MOE FP:ECFP4/FCFP4 archived columns carry multiplicity (count fingerprints, repeated keys in MOE 15-bit hash space, 0-32767; _2048 = mod-2048 fold of the same list); FP:MACCS is binary. The engine recomputes RDKit binary fingerprints from SMILES for both library and query and never imports any FP:* column.
btanimoto/ctanimoto are reference data only - they are NOT reproducible targets and the 26-vs-30 delta is not an error to fix: different fingerprint definition AND unknown MOE settings.
Subsets preserve their source ordering: sharedIds and absentFromRdkit26 follow her given order; notInAnna30 follows the engine result order (similarity desc).
Pyxis reported result was quoted by the product owner from the Pyxis UI; the 2026-09-12 live re-run of morgan/tanimoto @0.3 reproduced it exactly (26 hits, 13 shared with her list).
The engine echoes the canonicalized query as query_smiles O=C1CCC2NCCCC2N1 - the same molecule as Anna's reported string.
